tagline: Peat, casks and age statements: the language of the world's most collected spirit.
why: Whisky is a favourite of business dinners, bars and gift-giving in Hong Kong, where Macallan and Japanese whisky are status symbols. Whisky lovers talk about regions, cask types, age and smoky 'peat', and many collect rare bottles. Learn the main styles and a few distilleries and you can order well, appreciate a gift, and enjoy a conversation at the bar.

essentials.title: Whisky vs whiskey
essentials.body: Scotland, Japan and Canada spell it 'whisky'; Ireland and the US usually use 'whiskey'.

essentials.title: Single malt vs blended
essentials.body: Single malt is made from malted barley at one distillery. Blended whisky mixes malts and grain whisky, like Johnnie Walker. Single malts are the connoisseur's focus.

essentials.title: Scotland's regions
essentials.body: Speyside (fruity, elegant: Macallan, Glenfiddich), Islay (smoky, peaty: Laphroaig, Lagavulin, Ardbeg), Highlands (varied), Lowlands (light) and Campbeltown (briny).

essentials.title: Casks shape flavour
essentials.body: Most flavour comes from the oak barrel. Ex-bourbon casks give vanilla; sherry casks give dried fruit and spice.

essentials.title: Age statements
essentials.body: A 12-year-old whisky spent at least 12 years in the cask. Older isn't always better, but it's rarer and pricier.

essentials.title: American whiskey
essentials.body: Bourbon must be mostly corn and aged in new charred oak, giving sweet caramel notes. Rye is spicier.

essentials.title: Japanese whisky
essentials.body: Modelled on Scotch but famously refined; Yamazaki and Hibiki became so popular that age-statement bottles ran short.

names.name: The Macallan
names.what: Speyside's luxury giant; its rare bottles set auction records and dominate Hong Kong gifting.

names.name: Johnnie Walker
names.what: The world's best-selling Scotch, a blend; Blue Label is a classic gift.

names.name: Yamazaki
names.what: Japan's first malt distillery, owned by Suntory.

names.name: Nikka
names.what: Japan's other big whisky house; Yoichi and Miyagikyo distilleries.

names.name: Karuizawa
names.what: Closed Japanese distillery whose bottles are prized collectibles.

names.name: Buffalo Trace / Pappy Van Winkle
names.what: Bourbon distillery; Pappy is the hardest-to-find bourbon.

names.name: Masataka Taketsuru
names.what: Father of Japanese whisky, who learned in Scotland.

names.name: Kavalan
names.what: Taiwanese whisky that shocked the world by winning top awards.

timeline.event: Earliest written record of Scotch whisky.
Nikka's Yoichi wins 'Best of the Best' at a global tasting.
Yamazaki Sherry Cask named world's best whisky, sparking a Japanese whisky frenzy.
Another Macallan 1926 sells for £2.1 million, a record.
Hong Kong cuts duty on spirits priced above HK$200.

now.headline: Whisky boom cools
now.detail: After a decade of rising prices, collector demand and secondary prices for many bottles have softened.

now.headline: Japanese whisky rules
now.detail: Japan introduced rules in 2024 defining 'Japanese whisky' after some brands sold imported blends.

now.headline: New world whisky
now.detail: Taiwan, India, Australia and England produce award winners.

now.headline: Highballs everywhere
now.detail: Lighter whisky drinks are popular with younger drinkers.

local.headline: Duty cut
local.detail: Since 2024 the duty on spirits over HK$200 is only 10% on the portion above HK$200, aimed at making Hong Kong a spirits trading hub.

local.headline: Gift culture
local.detail: Macallan, Johnnie Walker Blue and Hibiki are classic Chinese New Year and business gifts.

local.headline: Whisky bars
local.detail: Speakeasies in Central and Sheung Wan rank among Asia's best bars.

local.headline: Auctions
local.detail: Hong Kong hosts major whisky auctions by Sotheby's and Bonhams.

debates.question: Water or no water?
debates.sides: Purists say neat; many experts add a few drops to open aromas.

debates.question: Is ice a crime?
debates.sides: Ice dulls flavour, but it's your drink. Japanese culture embraces it.

debates.question: Is older better?
debates.sides: Older is rarer; younger can be more vibrant.

debates.question: Should you drink or collect?
debates.sides: Collectors invest; purists say whisky is meant to be opened.
